name: ShadowFi SDF unauthenticated burn(address,uint256)
summary: ShadowFi's SDF token declares burn(address account, uint256 _amount) public with no owner check, no allowance check and no msg.sender == account check; it simply calls _transferFrom(account, DEAD, _amount). The attacker deployed a one-shot contract that bought 0.010354936721195452 SDF from the PancakeSwap SDF/WBNB pair 0xf9e3151e813cd6729d52d9a0c3ee69f22cce650a with 0.001 WBNB, called SDF.burn(pair, 10354936721195451) to destroy the pair's entire SDF reserve except one wei, called pair.sync() so the reserves became 1 wei SDF against 1,078.615699417903036883 WBNB, and then swapped 8.461538283 SDF for 1,078.616699290110670619 WBNB before selfdestructing.
notes: Top-level creation of the immutable SDF token by 0x5671e238bee4cd57a5722038f846f35d8ca35ed7; the constructor also created the SDF/WBNB pair. The 18,501-byte runtime is byte-identical at block 20771762 and block 20969095 and the contract has no proxy or upgrade mechanism.

Single-transaction exploit. The victim is the PancakeSwap SDF/WBNB pair 0xf9e3151e813cd6729d52d9a0c3ee69f22cce650a and its liquidity providers. Its WBNB balance went from 1,078.615699417903036883 before the transaction to 127,792,366,264 wei after, a depletion of 1,078.615699290110670619 WBNB, which is also exactly the 1,078.616699290110670619 WBNB the attacker received minus the 0.001 WBNB he seeded, so the attacker-supplied input is excluded. The 10,354,936.721195451 SDF burned out of the same pair is not valued separately: its only market was this pool, so pricing it would double-count the WBNB leg, and the burn made it unsellable. Gas is not deducted and there was no recovery; the attacker unwrapped the WBNB in the next block and moved it out in 26 transactions to 0x0d5550d52428e7e3175bfc9550207e4ad3859b17.
